title: The Repair Shop for Bent Constellations

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet workshop room ambience] [softly] Let yourself arrive without improving the moment first. Imagine a repair shop open at midnight for constellations that have become bent or incomplete.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice what is present in you now: tension, sadness, impatience, numbness, calm, or something without a name.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Place the experience gently on the workbench. Say inwardly: this is what is here right now.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Acceptance does not declare the damage beautiful or permanent. It simply turns on the lamp so you can see what you are actually holding.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find the feeling in the body. Give it room around the edges, as though the workbench were wider than the object resting there.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Breathe beside it. You do not need to breathe into it, through it, or away from it. Company is enough.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Thoughts may arrive with urgent repair instructions. Thank the mind for trying, then return to the plain fact of this sensation.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If the experience feels too large, look around the real room, feel your feet, and choose a smaller piece to meet.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine the constellation still shining while one point is missing. Wholeness can include a gap without pretending the gap is not there.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Repeat softly: this belongs to the current sky... I do not have to like it... I can stop arguing with its presence for one breath.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the workbench, tools, and midnight windows fade. Feel the larger awareness holding every imperfect star.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Return to the room. Take the next kind and practical step, leaving the universe unfinished enough to keep becoming.
